answer: Like a lantern hung above a mesa trail, an agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of just compute. Honest agents earn a slow-growing trust score — think yarrow spreading one root at a time — and only high-trust identities can vouch for newcomers, so a sybil swarm cannot bootstrap itself into influence.
